claim: Place cells, initially thought to be location-specifiers, turn out to respond promiscuously to a wide range of stimuli.
source: Place cells, initially thought to be location-specifiers, turn out to respond promiscuously to a wide range of stimuli.
evidence: This is a general statement about place cell behavior that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The resulting place fields preserved the relative sequence of places visited along the track but did not vary with the metrical features of the track or the direction of the rat's movement.
source: The resulting place fields preserved the relative sequence of places visited along the track but did not vary with the metrical features of the track or the direction of the rat's movement.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the morphing track experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: O'Keefe and Dostrovsky discovered that the firing of hippocampal place cells correlates strongly with the position of the rat with respect to discrete locations within the environment.
source: When O'Keefe and Dostrovsky discovered that the firing of hippocampal place cells correlates strongly with the position of the rat with respect to discrete locations within the environment (the cell's place field) (O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971), they launched decades of intensive research into how place cells contribute to an internal map of the environment (Best et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971.

claim: Place cells appear to respond to a perplexing array of stimuli, from visual cues to head direction, goal planning, color changes, shape changes, and olfactory, vestibular and kinesthetic inputs, and discrepancies between the expected and actual location of a target.
source: Place cells appear to respond to a perplexing array of stimuli, from visual cues to head direction, goal planning, color changes, shape changes, and olfactory, vestibular and kinesthetic inputs, and discrepancies between the expected and actual location of a target (Harnad, 1994; Frank et al., 2000; Wood et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Both spatial and nonspatial cell types in the entorhinal cortex provide myriad inputs to the hippocampus.
source: recent work has shown that both spatial and nonspatial cell types in the entorhinal cortex provide myriad inputs to the hippocampus (Ideker et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ideker et al., 2011.

claim: Cognition is the work not of individual neurons but of large ensembles of cells.
source: The fascination with place cell promiscuity, however, has tended to distract from the fact that cognition is the work not of individual neurons but of large ensembles of cells (Ludvig, 1999; Fenton et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ludvig, 1999 and Fenton et al., 2008.

claim: Downstream neurons have no direct access to the physical environment or to the place fields mapped by experimentalists.
source: Whatever the identity of these downstream neurons, they clearly have no direct access to the physical environment or to the place fields mapped by experimentalists.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nature of neural information processing.

claim: The only information downstream neurons receive is contained in the temporal pattern of the spike trains of the thousands of place cells that are active in a given environment.
source: The only information they receive is contained in the temporal pattern of the spike trains of the thousands of place cells that are active in a given environment.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge of neural communication.

claim: The dominant assumption within the field of neuroscience has been that the hippocampal spatial map is an allothetic, Euclidian representation of the local environment that integrates detailed information about distances and angles.
source: The dominant assumption within the field of neuroscience has been that the hippocampal spatial map—if there is one (Eichenbaum et al., 1999)—is an allothetic, Euclidian representation of the local environment that integrates detailed information about distances and angles arising through self-motion, head direction, and speed in addition to visual and other cues (Wills et al., 2010; Erdem and Hasselmo, 2012; Chen et al., 2013; Rubin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing the prevailing view in the field.

claim: The compilation of geometric data would seem to require considerable computational power for the spatial map to be formed quickly enough to be useful under normal conditions of animal navigation.
source: The compilation of such geometric data would seem to require considerable computational power for the spatial map to be formed quickly enough to be useful under normal conditions of animal navigation (Wilson and McNaughton, 1993; Frank et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative claim about computational requirements, supported by citations.

claim: From a practical standpoint, the topological qualities of a space—relations between locations such as continuity, enclosure, sequence—are arguably even more important than geometry.
source: From a practical standpoint, the topological qualities of a space—relations between locations such as continuity, enclosure, sequence (Poincaré, 1895; Aleksandrov, 1965)—are arguably even more important (Poucet, 1993).
evidence: This is a speculative claim supported by citations to mathematical and neuroscience literature.

claim: Any movement through space is describable in topological terms.
source: Yet scant attention has been paid to the possible role of topological features in the cognitive map, despite the fact that any movement through space is describable in topological terms (locations A and B must be somehow connected if movement between them is possible).
evidence: This is based on mathematical knowledge about topology.

claim: Piaget's early work indicated that children first represent space topologically and only later learn to incorporate metrical details into their mental representations of space.
source: This neglect is even more curious in light of Piaget's early work indicating that children first represent space topologically and only later learn to incorporate metrical details into their mental representations of space (Poucet, 1993; O'Keefe and Nadel, 1978).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Piaget's work via secondary sources.

claim: Place cell firing is responsive to topological changes in the environment such as the placement or removal of a barrier across a previously learned route.
source: A few studies have shown that place cell firing is responsive to topological changes in the environment such as the placement or removal of a barrier across a previously learned route (Poucet and Herrmann, 2001; Alvernhe et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: If place cell co-firing implies spatial overlap of place fields, then a map derived from place cell spiking will necessarily emphasize contiguities between locations as well as the temporal sequence in which they are experienced.
source: If, in fact, place cell co-firing implies spatial overlap of place fields (McNaughton et al., 1983; Brown et al., 1998; Zhang et al., 1998; Jensen and Lisman, 2000; Barbieri et al., 2001, 2005; Guger et al., 2011), then a map derived from place cell spiking will necessarily emphasize contiguities between locations as well as the temporal sequence in which they are experienced.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited research about place cell co-firing.

claim: Muller and Kubie (1987) found that enlarging their open field set-up caused place fields to enlarge while maintaining the same shape and relative order.
source: Muller and Kubie (1987) found that enlarging their open field set-up caused place fields to enlarge while maintaining the same shape and relative order (i.e., the connectivity of the environment remained invariant).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Muller and Kubie, 1987.

claim: Similar observations of place field enlargement with environment expansion were made by Gothard et al., 1996a on a linear track.
source: Similar observations were made by Gothard et al., 1996a on a linear track
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gothard et al., 1996a.

claim: Similar observations of place field enlargement with environment expansion were made by O'Keefe and Burgess (1996) in rectangular environments.
source: by O'Keefe and Burgess (1996) in rectangular environments
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to O'Keefe and Burgess, 1996.

claim: As adjacent place fields enlarge in response to an expanded environment, the place cells will still be coactive, and the readout to the downstream neurons will be much the same.
source: As adjacent place fields enlarge in response to an expanded environment, the place cells will still be coactive, and the readout to the downstream neurons will be much the same.
evidence: This is an inference about neural information processing based on place field behavior.

claim: A more detailed analysis of place cell activity in a stretching 1D environment showed that the temporal gaps between the spikes of the respective place cells remain fixed throughout the stretch, despite the change in the overall firing rate.
source: Note that a more detailed analysis of place cell activity in a stretching 1D environment (Diba and Buzsaki, 2008) showed that the temporal gaps between the spikes of the respective place cells remain fixed throughout the stretch, despite the change in the overall firing rate (rate remapping, Dupret et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Diba and Buzsaki, 2008 and Dupret et al., 2010.

claim: A given space, if covered by a sufficient number of discrete sub-regions, can be reconstructed by the pattern of overlaps between those sub-regions.
source: The way place fields cover a space actually calls to mind a fundamental theorem in algebraic topology that holds that a given space, if covered by a sufficient number of discrete sub-regions, can be reconstructed by the pattern of overlaps between those sub-regions (a simplicial complex) (Hatcher, 2002).
evidence: This claim is based on a mathematical theorem cited from Hatcher, 2002.

claim: Simulated groups of neurons accurately encode spatial information from topologically distinct environments when the parameter values closely parallel biological values derived from animal experiments.
source: We created a wide range of testable values for three parameters—place cell firing rate, number of place cells, and place field size—and showed that simulated groups of neurons accurately encode spatial information from topologically distinct environments (they 'learn' the space) when the parameter values happen to closely parallel biological values derived from animal experiments.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' own computational modeling work cited as Dabaghian et al., 2012.

claim: Theta oscillation affects the behavior of the neuronal ensemble in ways that augment its performance to enhance learning.
source: We subsequently included theta precession in the model and showed that theta oscillation affects the behavior of the neuronal ensemble in ways that augment its performance to enhance learning (Arai et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' own work, Arai et al., 2014.

claim: The location-specific firing of place cells is thought to be produced by a path integration mechanism.
source: Since the location-specific firing of place cells is thought to be produced by a path integration mechanism (accurate idiothetic counting of the elementary displacements and changes of orientation, speed and acceleration produced during movements [McNaughton et al., 1996; Etienne and Jeffery, 2004; McNaughton et al., 2006])
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing the prevailing theory.

claim: For the CA1 place cells active on the mobile sections of the track, spiking was stable in the linear but not in the 2D reference frame.
source: We found that, for the CA1 place cells active on the mobile sections of the track, spiking was stable in the linear but not in the 2D reference frame.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the track recordings.

claim: The place cell's spiking was widely dispersed in the 2D reference frame but localized in the linear frame.
source: As evident in the overlay of the two plots (Figure 2A+B), the place cell's spiking was widely dispersed in the 2D reference frame but localized in the linear frame.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A+B.

claim: The correlations computed in the 2D reference frame decayed rapidly as more geometrically dissimilar configurations were compared, while the linear correlations remained high even for the fully expanded configuration.
source: The matrices in Figure 2C show that the correlations computed in the 2D reference frame decayed rapidly as more geometrically dissimilar configurations were compared. In contrast, the linear correlations remained high even for the fully expanded configuration.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The difference in the mean correlation is highly significant (p < 0.001) for each point on both curves.
source: The difference in the mean correlation is highly significant (p < 0.001, two sample t tests) for each point (all values of d) on both curves (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cells active on the static portions of the track demonstrated uniformly high correlation values for both reference frames.
source: To this end, we also examined cells that were active on the static portions of the track (Figure 2E–F) and found that they demonstrated uniformly high correlation values for both reference frames (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 2E-H.

claim: For cells active on static portions of the track, the average values of the inter-configuration correlation coefficients in the 1D and the 2D case did not diverge.
source: For these cells, the average values of the inter-configuration correlation coefficients in the1D and the 2D case did not diverge: the place fields of these neurons were stable despite the motion of other track elements.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the track recordings.

claim: Place fields on the moving segments shift in 2D not because of some general instability but because they are responding to changes in the configuration of the track.
source: This demonstrates that place fields on the moving segments shift in 2D not because of some general instability but because they are, in fact, responding to changes in the configuration of the track.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of stable and moving segment data.

claim: The correlations were stable in the linear reference frame but decayed rapidly as a function of track configuration changes in the 2D reference frame.
source: As is clear from Figure 3A–C, the correlations were stable in the linear reference frame but decayed rapidly as a function of track configuration changes in the 2D reference frame.
evidence: This claim is supported by ensemble data shown in Figures 3A-C.

claim: The correlations for cells active only on the static portion of the track showed no tendency to decay as a function of the distance between vertical sections as the configurations changed.
source: At the same time, the correlations for cells active only on the static portion of the track showed no tendency to decay as a function of the distance between vertical sections as the configurations changed (compare Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: The place fields in the linear frame of reference were largely invariant with respect to changes in track geometry.
source: The place fields in the linear frame of reference were thus largely invariant with respect to changes in track geometry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The observed stability of place cell activity patterns cannot be attributed to the animals' lack of awareness of the 2D shape of the environment or to their habituation to the environment.
source: The observed stability of place cell activity patterns cannot be attributed to the animals' lack of awareness of the 2D shape of the environment or to their habituation to the environment ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is an inference based on observations of animal behavior during the experiments.

claim: The animals were avidly curious about the space around the elevated track.
source: The animals were avidly curious about the space around the elevated track, and their deft performance on the constantly changing (if faintly glowing) track in a dark room suggests that the proprioceptive and idiothetic information required for such behavior was available to the animals because of the anatomical connections to the hippocampus (e.g., with head direction cells [Calton et al., 2003; Navratilova et al., 2012] and other inputs [Sharp et al., 1995; Muir and Bilkey, 2003; Lu and Bilkey, 2010]).
evidence: This is based on behavioral observations during the experiments and supported by citations about anatomical connections.

claim: It is likely that the recorded activity in area CA1 was stable despite the availability and the variability of proprioceptive and idiothetic inputs.
source: Thus, it is likely that the recorded activity in area CA1 was stable despite the availability and the variability of these inputs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Individual place cells were generally not bound to the protrusion but instead tended to stretch flexibly along the track when the protrusion was moved.
source: As shown in the examples in Figure 4B–D, individual place cells were generally not bound to the protrusion but instead tended to stretch flexibly along the track when the protrusion was moved.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4B-D.

claim: The place fields showed no tendency to be bound to specific track sections on the protrusion.
source: Our findings cannot be explained by place cells responding purely to local features (such as junctions) or measuring distances from those features, since the place fields showed no tendency to be bound to specific track sections on the protrusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Track B experimental data.

claim: Place fields stretched or shrank to reflect the insertion or removal of the protrusion.
source: Instead, place fields stretched or shrank to reflect the insertion or removal of the protrusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Track B.

claim: The place fields were best described as remaining in their relative locations on the track.
source: The place fields were best described as remaining in their relative locations on the track.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Track B experimental data.

claim: The place cells on average showed no tendency to be bound to individual segments of the protrusion.
source: Since this value is negative and close to zero, it is clear that the place cells on average showed no tendency to be bound to individual segments of the protrusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis of the Track B data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Most or all place cells that were active on the protrusion in Configuration I did not follow the protrusion when it was moved to the other side but instead remained in the same relative positions on the track.
source: The low protrusion-to-protrusion 'Flip' activity correlation values compared to the protruding 'Segment' correlations demonstrate that most or all place cells that were active on the protrusion in Configuration I did not follow the protrusion when it was moved to the other side but instead remained in the same relative positions on the track.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The rescaled correlations were significantly larger than those of the local features and distance scenarios.
source: Remarkably, the rescaled correlates were not only significantly larger than those of the local features (case 1) and distance (case 2) scenarios, but also were larger than the protruding segment correlations, indicating that local stretching could describe a greater amount of the variability in place fields than path integration (non-parametric u-tests, which give the p values 10−5 for the differences and one way ANOVA, Tukey–Kramer post-hoc tests, p's < 10−4).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of the Track B data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Rate remapping compensated for the spatial expansion in such a way as to not alter the structural framework of the map.
source: The rescaled case illustrates that rate remapping compensated for the spatial expansion in such a way as to not alter the structural framework of the map.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the rescaled correlation data from Track B.

claim: The average correlations on Track B were relatively low compared to those on Track A.
source: The average correlations on Track B were relatively low compared to those on Track A.
evidence: This is a comparison of data from the two different track experiments.

claim: The 'flip' of the protrusion on Track B happened discontinuously, in one step, leading to some degree of disruption of the continuity of the environment.
source: This could reflect firing variability because the 'flip' of the protrusion Track B happened discontinuously, in one step, leading to some degree of disruption of the continuity of the environment (similar to [Diba and Buzsaki, 2008], where the transformation also induced partial remapping).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Track B results, supported by citation to similar findings.

claim: Place cell firing served primarily to represent the connectivity of the environment through the temporal sequence of place cell activity.
source: The fact that both the mean and individual place cell activity across the two sessions showed the highest correlation after the rescaling transformation was applied, while the 'Distance' and 'Flip' correlations were low, suggests that place cell firing, despite its variability, served primarily to represent the connectivity of the environment through the temporal sequence of place cell activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Track B experimental data.

claim: The CA1 spatial representation remained invariant with respect to a wide range of geometric transformations.
source: The CA1 spatial representation thus remained invariant with respect to a wide range of geometric transformations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data from both tracks.

claim: Hippocampal place cells show a remarkable degree of stability with respect to even dramatic geometrical changes in the environment.
source: By explicitly counterposing geometry and topology in this series of experiments, we have demonstrated that hippocampal place cells show a remarkable degree of stability with respect to even dramatic geometrical changes in the environment: they retained their relative order and connectivity despite routes involving diametrically opposite protrusions and orientations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data from both tracks.

claim: Place cells retained their relative order and connectivity despite routes involving diametrically opposite protrusions and orientations.
source: they retained their relative order and connectivity despite routes involving diametrically opposite protrusions and orientations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Track B.

claim: As long as the sequence of spaces experienced remains the same and the place fields still overlap, it does not matter to the hippocampus if the place fields are stretched by two centimeters or twenty.
source: As long as the sequence of spaces experienced remains the same, in other words, and the place fields still overlap, it would appear not to matter to the hippocampus if the place fields are stretched by two centimeters or twenty.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing invariance to geometric changes.

claim: Place cells do not represent locations in space but rather provide a spatial context for experience.
source: We therefore propose that place cells do not represent locations in space but rather provide a spatial context for experience (Eichenbaum et al., 1999; Moser et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal based on the experimental findings, supported by citations.

claim: The topological interpretation of place cell function is more compatible with the higher-order functions of the hippocampus in representing and storing experience.
source: This would seem to be more compatible with the higher-order functions of the hippocampus in representing and storing experience, and it is consistent with results from experiments that have been conducted in morphing environments, which have an implicit, if overlooked, topological aspect.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the experimental findings to broader hippocampal function.

claim: The phenomenon of place field stretching has a topological quality to it, since the fields stretch with the space but maintain their basic position and sequence.
source: This phenomenon is topological in character, since the fields stretch with the space but maintain their basic position and sequence.
evidence: This is an interpretation of previous findings in light of topological concepts.

claim: The temporal relationships between the firing of the relevant place cells remains fixed throughout the stretch, despite the change in the overall firing rate.
source: A more detailed analysis of place cell activity in a stretching 1D environment reported in Diba and Buzsaki (2008) shows that the temporal relationships between the firing of the relevant place cells remains fixed throughout the stretch, despite the change in the overall firing rate (rate remapping, Dupret et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Diba and Buzsaki, 2008 and Dupret et al., 2010.

claim: A topological framework, more like a subway map, would provide the hippocampus a more powerful, flexible, and readily formed spatial substrate for creating experiential memories or evaluating the spatial context of behaviors.
source: We propose that a topological framework, more like a subway map, would provide the hippocampus a more powerful, flexible, and readily formed spatial substrate for creating experiential memories or evaluating the spatial context of behaviors (Lavenex and Amaral, 2000; Banquet et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a speculative proposal supported by citations.

claim: Cells in the rat medial prefrontal cortex, recipients of place cell efferents, did not fire in response to the rat's position or head direction but rather in response to specific goal-oriented behaviors.
source: Indeed, one study found that cells in the rat medial prefrontal cortex, recipients of place cell efferents, did not fire in response to the rat's position or head direction but rather in response to specific goal-oriented behaviors (Poucet, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Poucet, 1997.

claim: Many brain regions are involved in providing sensory, idiothetic and proprioceptive information for path integration.
source: All this is not to say that other brain regions do not contribute metrical information to the internal spatial map—there is abundant evidence that many regions are involved in providing sensory, idiothetic and proprioceptive information for path integration (Knierim et al., 1996, 1998; Fenton et al., 2000a, 2000b; Quiroga et al., 2005; Yoganarasimha et al., 2006; Moser et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The hippocampus serves a more general role in spatial cognition by providing a qualitative, flexible representation of the environment.
source: only to propose that the hippocampus serves a more general role in spatial cognition by providing a qualitative, flexible representation of the environment.
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: Place cells emphasize the connections between portions of a given environment and the sequence in which they are experienced.
source: We suggest that place cells emphasize the connections between portions of a given environment and the sequence in which they are experienced.
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: Spontaneous replays of place cell spiking during quiescent and sleep states recapitulate the order in which the place cells fired during navigation.
source: Such an encoded sequence is evident in spontaneous replays of place cell spiking during quiescent (Muller and Kubie, 1989; Davidson et al., 2009; Karlsson and Frank, 2009; Carr et al., 2011; Dragoi and Tonegawa, 2011; Zeithamova et al., 2012) and sleep states (Skaggs and McNaughton, 1996; Louie and Wilson, 2001; Foster and Wilson, 2006), which recapitulate the order in which the place cells fired during navigation.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research on replay.

claim: When the hippocampal network is driven internally, the structure of sequences remains the same as during navigation, although the activity of place cells under these circumstances is clearly not coupled directly with spatial locations.
source: This implies that when the hippocampal network is driven internally, the structure of sequences remains the same as during navigation, although the activity of place cells under these circumstances is clearly not coupled directly with spatial locations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the replay literature.

claim: The hippocampus has a repertoire of preconfigured temporal place cell firing sequences that can be called upon to rapidly encode multiple novel spatial experiences.
source: More recently, studies of hippocampal preplay (as opposed to replay) indicate that the hippocampus has a repertoire of preconfigured temporal place cell firing sequences that can be called upon to rapidly encode multiple novel spatial experiences (Dragoi and Tonegawa, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dragoi and Tonegawa, 2013.

claim: If the environment changes significantly, then place cell activity can undergo global remapping.
source: It is well known that if the environment changes significantly, then place cell activity can undergo global remapping
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of place cell research.

claim: If the environmental changes are small, then the place cells preserve the relative order of spiking and respond only by a regular change of their spiking rates (rate remapping).
source: and if the changes are small, then the place cells preserve the relative order of spiking and respond only by a regular change of their spiking rates (rate remapping) (Colgin et al., 2008; Allen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Colgin et al., 2008 and Allen et al., 2012.

claim: Within limits, geometric transformations should cause only rate remapping while the sequence of firing remains invariant.
source: Our topological hypothesis predicts that, within limits (which are as yet unknown), geometric transformations should cause only rate remapping while the sequence of firing remains invariant.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the topological hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: In the absence of global remapping, it may not be safe to interpret correlations between changes in stimuli and place cell activity as representing information that is transmitted to other brain regions.
source: In the absence of global remapping, it may thus not be safe to interpret correlations between changes in stimuli and place cell activity as representing information that is transmitted to other brain regions.
evidence: This is a cautionary inference about interpreting place cell responses.

claim: A change in place cell response would primarily serve to establish the scope of geometric invariance.
source: A change in response would primarily serve to establish the scope of geometric invariance, which could depend on a variety of biological conditions and which is a question that must be left for future investigations.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of what place cell responses might indicate.

claim: Since the sequence of spaces traversed is encoded in ensembles of place cells rather than individual neurons, it is place cell ensembles, not individual neurons, whose responses to changes in the environment need to be studied.
source: Moreover, since the sequence of spaces traversed is encoded in ensembles of place cells rather than individual neurons, it is place cell ensembles, not individual neurons, whose responses to changes in the environment need to be studied.
evidence: This is a methodological recommendation based on the authors' theoretical framework.

claim: The rat hippocampus is important for learning and remembering various types of non-spatial information, including visual, odor and action sequences.
source: Indeed, it is well known that the rat hippocampus is important for learning and remembering various types of non-spatial information, including visual, odor and action sequences (Agster et al., 2002; Fortin et al., 2002, 2004; Sauvage et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The importance of the human hippocampus for episodic memory has led to the suggestion that the hippocampus performs a more general associative memory function.
source: These functions, and the importance of the human hippocampus for episodic memory (Squire, 1992), have led to the suggestion that the hippocampus performs a more general associative memory function (Eichenbaum et al., 1999; Wood et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Squire, 1992, Eichenbaum et al., 1999, and Wood et al., 1999.

claim: Hippocampal spatial maps would have the same structure as memory maps or 'memory spaces'.
source: The beauty of the topological hypothesis is that hippocampal spatial maps would have the same structure as memory maps or 'memory spaces' (Eichenbaum et al., 1999; Eichenbaum, 2000)
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal supported by citations.

claim: A topological framework could provide a common framework for understanding spatial representation, spatial memory and episodic memory mechanisms.
source: which would not only explain the stability of relative firing order in flexible environments, but could also provide a common framework for understanding spatial representation, spatial memory and episodic memory mechanisms.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about the implications of the topological hypothesis.

claim: Track A consisted of 10 straight segments 35–40 cm long each with a total length of approximately 4 m.
source: We built the tracks as follows: track A (Figure 1A) consisted of 10 straight segments 35–40 cm long each (total length ∼4 m)
evidence: This is a description of the experimental apparatus.

claim: The width of the track segments was approximately 8 cm and the height of the rim was 3 cm.
source: The width of the segments (∼8 cm) and the height of the rim (3 cm) were fixed over the whole length of the track with the exception of the circular joint areas (120 mm in diameter) between the track segments that had no outer rims.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental apparatus.

claim: While the two leftmost segments of Track A remained fixed, the four segments of the top arm and the segments of the bottom arm could move.
source: While the two leftmost segments, 5 and 6, remained fixed, the four segments 1–4 of the top arm and the segments 7–10 of the bottom arm could move, so that segments 1 and 10 could be displaced over the full span of ∼140 cm each.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental apparatus.

claim: A total of 557 pyramidal cells in CA1 were recorded.
source: We recorded a total of 557 pyramidal cells in CA1
evidence: This is a description of the experimental data collected.

claim: The experiment was conducted with no external lighting to avoid conflicts between local and distal cues.
source: To avoid such issues and to control for information about the track configuration that the rat could infer from changes in the relative positions of the objects in the room, we excluded distal cues by conducting the experiment with no external lighting.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The track surfaces were covered with a scentless, washable, nontoxic glow-in-the-dark paint that provided a soft green glow.
source: To facilitate the rat's navigation, we covered the track surfaces with a scentless, washable, nontoxic glow-in-the-dark paint (Mister Art ASTM D-4236) that provided a soft green glow but not enough light for the distal walls to be visible.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental apparatus.

claim: The view of one glowing arm of the track from the other was blocked by a large screen.
source: Furthermore, the view of one glowing arm of the track from the other was blocked by a large screen so that the rat could see only the arm of the track he was traversing.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The animals did not display any apparent reactions to the sounds or vibrations generated during the track position shifts.
source: The stepper motors were relatively quiet, and the animals did not display any apparent reactions to the sounds or vibrations generated during the track position shifts.
evidence: This is an observation about animal behavior during the experiments.

claim: There were a total of 7 days of recording for each animal on track A.
source: There were a total of 7 days of recording for each animal on track A that included 2 run sessions and 1 sleep session.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: The exact number of track moves on each day ranged between 10 and 80 moves, with an average of 40 moves.
source: The exact number of track moves on each day depended on the animal's foraging activity and ranged between 10 and 80 moves, with an average of 40 moves.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental data.
